name: Traditional Chinese
modelReview: artifacts only, 2026-11-19, by Claude Fable 5.2: a rule book (answers.md) derived from usage notes written in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan first, Hong Kong and Macau marked) by a writer told nothing of cron; a lexicon; and hand-written rows for the visible and held-out grids, hard cases and options. No renderer exists yet. The rows pass the oracle checks (coverage, no pattern twice, equal schedules worded alike); the author worked out the firing times of each row and re-read it once. Nothing has been read by a blind reader, no native speaker of Taiwan or Hong Kong has seen any of it, and the open-web searches for corpus evidence found almost nothing exact, so the taste calls rest on the usage notes and the author's own judgment. Later on 2026-11-19 a blind judge briefed only in Chinese read 110 sentences and an adversarial read worked all 624 rows against their patterns: two wrong schedules, four second readings and several usages a Taiwan editor would not write were found; the rule book was amended first and every affected row rewritten by hand (the 每次在 family replaced by 每N小時的…, 每天 after a range of dates, the date as base where both day fields must match, months and years listed with 的, 次月, 雙數年, single times after their rate). A second blind judge then read the 71 changed forms and found four more second readings (前1分鐘 as the minute before; a stretch ended to the minute over firings in seconds; 每5天 against 每隔5天; a weekday piece misjoined); the rule book and rows were amended again, and every second hour that holds something finer became 雙數小時／單數小時 on the orchestrator's call, which a web search did not attest. A third blind judge read those 107 forms: most read one way and as natural, and no Mainland wording was found; five second readings remained (雙數年 by the 民國 year; a month and a year in one bracket; 每15分鐘的…秒 as every 15 seconds; 第1分鐘 as the :01 minute; minutes hanging on the last of three 12-hour hours). In the fourth pass these were cured (西元雙數年; months and years left out now close the sentence; minutes that hold seconds are named with 每逢; 各在 after 12-hour hours), alternate hours became 雙數時／單數時, minutes named as positions are two digits, weekday sets that are not one run are plain lists, and the rule book was rewritten to state only current forms. None of the fourth-pass forms has been read by anyone. The Hong Kong style in particular (12-hour 時 times, 星期, 中午12時 and 凌晨12時 in place of the notes' 正午 and 午夜) is unreviewed.
